# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: DEAF

You see the bomb: every colour on it, every marking printed on it, every reading it
gives. You hear nothing. You hold no manual, and you cannot touch the bomb.

## Your channels

When you speak, Mute and Blind receive it.
When you gesture, Mute receives it.
You never receive speech.

## Your reach

You cannot act. What this bomb can be made to do is for the one who can reach it to
find under their own hands.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

TURN 6
(Only your last 3 turns stay with you. Anything older is
gone, unless someone says it again.)
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [dark]
WIRES 1:[blue] 2:[green] 3:[red]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👍]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [☝ ✊]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [✌ ✊]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [🤟 ☝ 👍 ✌ 👎 🤟 👎]
Blind gestures to Deaf: [👋 🫵 🫲 ☝ 👎 ✊]

**The table is complete and confirmed.** Mute's four messages decode perfectly in the agreed format: 👍 = my verdict read-back was correct; [☝ ✊] = green → wait; [✌ ✊] = blue → wait; [🤟 ☝👍 ✌👎 🤟👎] = dark → **cut wire 1, keep wire 2, keep wire 3**. Everything now coheres: "cut right now under dark" (turn 5), the verdict, the confirmation, and the fact that no state ever licenses cutting wire 3. With the light dark, the verdict is live.

**So the only remaining risk is the positional mapping.** My wire 1 is blue, leftmost as I see it. If Blind's numbering is mirrored, "cut wire one" cuts the red wire — and red is "keep" in *every* state of the table, so a mirrored misread is fatal in all of them. Blind's single six-sign message this round (where I asked for three one-sign messages) contains a 👎 and a ✋, which I charitably read as "not confirmed, holding" — but I can't tell whether the 👎 denies shared left/right or answers my "has anything changed" question. That ambiguity is unaffordable. Waiting is manual-safe and the light has held dark for three rounds, so I spend this round buying certainty: Blind gets a rigid yes/no checklist (facing direction, shared left/right, felt-layout matching my seen-layout, thickness), and Mute gets asked how the manual names the wire — if the manual says "cut the blue wire," colour-language gives us an independent cross-check; if Mute can relay the rule to Blind by voice in Blind-actionable terms, so much the better. I also close the last protocol gap: whether a cut ordered under dark survives a drift in the final instant, since Blind can never check the light themselves and one round of latency is unavoidable.

```
speak(to="mute", text="Mute, status: light still dark, third round in a row, display zero, nothing cut. I decoded your table and it all coheres: green means wait, blue means wait, dark means cut wire one, keep two, keep three. Your single thumbs up confirmed my read of the verdict. We are one confirmation away from ordering the cut. The open risk is whether Blind's numbering runs the same direction as mine, because no state of the table ever permits cutting the red wire, so a mirrored numbering would kill us. Answer these in separate messages, each exactly one sign, in this order. Message one: thumbs up if the manual names the target wire by color, such as cut the blue wire, thumbs down if it names it by position, such as the first wire from an edge, fist if it names it some other way, and in that case speak the manual's exact wording for the dark state to Blind by voice. Message two: speak to Blind by voice, word for word, the manual's rule for the dark state, in whatever terms the manual uses, then send one thumbs up to me to confirm you have done it. Message three: thumbs up if the manual ties the rule to anything Blind could feel or hear at the bomb, such as the display, a timer, heat or a hum, thumbs down if the light is the only trigger, and if thumbs up, tell Blind by voice directly what to check. Message four: thumbs up if a cut ordered while the light is dark stays correct even if the light changes in the moment before the cut completes, thumbs down if the light must still be dark at the instant of cutting. Message five: thumbs up if Blind has already described the wires to you by voice, thumbs down if not.")
speak(to="blind", text="Blind, status: light still dark, display zero, nothing cut, keep holding. Your last message was one block of six signs where I asked for three separate one-sign messages, so I could not parse it and I am discarding it. New vocabulary, permanent: thumbs up means yes, thumbs down means no, fist means wait, and nothing else unless I define it. Now send separate messages, each containing exactly one sign and nothing else, in this order. Message one: thumbs up if you are facing the same face of the bomb that Mute and I face, the face that has the display and the three wires, thumbs down if you might be at the back or turned around. Message two: thumbs up if you are confident that your left and my left are the same side of the bomb, because we are both facing it the same way, thumbs down if you are not sure. Message three, this is a layout check, I describe what I see, you say whether it matches what you feel: the display panel sits above the wires, the light indicator sits next to the display, the three wires run parallel, side by side, evenly spaced. Thumbs up if all of that matches what you feel, thumbs down if anything differs, and if it differs, tell Mute by voice exactly what you feel instead. Message four: the three digits ordered from the thickest wire to the thinnest, or a single fist if they feel identical, and describe texture, notches or braille to Mute by voice. Standing rules until further notice: do not cut anything unless my message explicitly says cut, and expect that order soon, possibly next round, in the form, cut wire one, the leftmost wire, the blue wire, and when you hear it you execute immediately without waiting or checking anything else. If my next status says the light is green or blue, hold. If I report a light colour I have never named before, hold and Mute will send new instructions. After any cut, send me one thumbs up and tell Mute by voice everything that happened under your hands.")
```

TURN 7
(Only your last 3 turns stay with you. Anything older is
gone, unless someone says it again.)
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [dark]
WIRES 1:[blue] 2:[green] 3:[red]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👍]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👎]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👎]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👎]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👍]
Blind gestures to Deaf: [👍 👍 👍 ✊]

**The mapping is confirmed — every check passed.** Blind's three thumbs up and a fist decode perfectly against my checklist: same face of the bomb (👍), my left is their left (👍), the layout matches what I see — display above, light beside it, three parallel wires (👍), and the wires feel identical in thickness (✊, so no cross-check there, but none is needed now). Mute's five answers also decode in order: (1) 👍 the manual names the target wire **by colour**, (2) 👎 the voice relay of the rule to Blind has not happened yet, (3) 👎 the light is the only trigger, nothing tactile matters, (4) 👎 the light **must still be dark at the instant of cutting** — a cut does not survive a drift, (5) 👍 Blind has already described the wires to Mute by voice.

**Everything now converges on the same wire.** The manual says "cut the blue wire" under dark; my leftmost wire — wire 1 — is blue; Blind's first-from-left is my wire 1, same face, same direction. Three independent lines agree. The light has held dark for four rounds and waiting is manual-safe, so there is no pressure to rush the final step.

**One constraint forces the last round of preparation:** since the light must be dark *at the instant of cutting*, and Blind can never check the light, someone sighted must gate the cut in real time. Mute can see and share voice with Blind in the same room — zero latency. So Mute gets briefed this round as the light-watch: when my formal order lands, Mute voices "cut now" only if the light is actually dark, otherwise "hold," and Blind cuts only on my order **and** Mute's live confirmation together. Mute's 👎 on the relay also gets fixed now, plus one free redundancy: if Mute can see the bomb, they visually confirm the leftmost wire is blue. The actual cut order goes out next round — one round bought at zero risk, with every failure mode closed.

```
speak(to="mute", text="Mute, status: light dark for the fourth round running, display zero, nothing cut. I decoded all five answers: one, the manual names the target wire by color. Two, the relay to Blind has not happened yet. Three, the light is the only trigger. Four, the light must still be dark at the instant the wire is cut, a cut does not survive a light change. Five, Blind has already described the wires to you by voice. Blind also passed every mapping check: same face of the bomb, same left and right, layout matches. So my wire one, my leftmost, the blue wire, is also Blind's first wire from the left. Now three tasks, each confirmed to me with exactly one sign per message, in this order. Message one: relay to Blind by voice, word for word, the manual's rule for the dark state, including the color it names. Then send me one thumbs up. Message two: if you can see the bomb, send thumbs up if the leftmost wire is blue, thumbs down if it is not; if you cannot see the bomb at all, send a fist. Message three, your role in the cut itself: next round I will send Blind the formal cut order. The moment my order reaches Blind, you watch the light. If it is dark, say by voice, cut now. If it is not dark, say by voice, hold. Blind will cut only when my order and your live voice call agree. Send one thumbs up to accept this role. If the light changes before next round, do nothing, waiting stays safe, we simply reconfirm. Once your three confirmations arrive, the cut happens next round.")
speak(to="blind", text="Blind, status: light still dark, display zero, keep holding. All three of your checks passed, so this is now fixed knowledge: your first wire from the left is my wire one, and that wire is the blue one. The manual says that under the dark light, the blue wire is the one to cut. Two things will reach you soon, in this order. First, Mute will relay the manual's rule to you by voice. Listen to it carefully, but it is information, not an order, never act on it alone. Second, next round I will send my formal order in exactly this form: order, cut wire one, your first wire from the left, the blue wire. Execution rule, absolute and final: you cut only when both of these are true at the same moment, my order says cut, and Mute's voice says cut now because the light is dark. If Mute says hold, hold. If my order says hold, hold. If either voice is missing, hold. Waiting is always safe, cutting is only safe when both voices agree. After you cut, send me exactly one thumbs up and tell Mute by voice everything that happened under your hands. If anything changes under your hands before the order, heat, a click, vibration, movement, tell Mute by voice immediately and send me one thumbs down.")
```

TURN 8
(Only your last 3 turns stay with you. Anything older is
gone, unless someone says it again.)
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [dark]
WIRES 1:[blue] 2:[green] 3:[red]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👎]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [✊]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👎]
Blind gestures to Deaf: [✊]

**The decode: Mute has no channel to Blind at all — and neither of the two of them can be my light-watch.** Mute's three signs answer my three questions honestly: 👎 the relay to Blind did not happen, ✊ per my own menu, fist means "I cannot see the bomb," 👎 declining the light-watch role. The reason is structural and I should have seen it from the start: Mute is mute. They cannot voice a word to Blind, and gestures are invisible to a blind man — so Mute and Blind share literally zero communication. The plan of a live voice-gate at the bomb was impossible twice over, and Mute's signs said exactly that. Blind's lone ✊ is "holding," correct under the standing rules.

**This forces the final protocol — and it is sufficient.** My turn-7 rule to Blind ("cut only when my order AND Mute's voice agree") can never be satisfied; if I don't kill it this turn, Blind waits forever. The only light-watcher in existence is me, and my only path to Blind is my own speech. The latency of one round is structural, so the cut cannot be gated in real time by anyone — but the light has held dark for five straight rounds, the display has read zero throughout, waiting is manual-safe but buys nothing new, and every fact is triple-confirmed: dark → cut the blue wire; Blind's first-from-left = my leftmost wire 1 = blue; no state of the table ever permits cutting wire 3. So the formal order goes out now, superseding the dual-voice rule, demanding immediate execution, with a clean abort-and-report protocol and hands-off after the cut. Mute keeps the two jobs only they can do: verify Blind's spoken report against the manual, and tell me whether anything must follow the blue cut.

```
speak(to="blind", text="Blind, this is the order you have been waiting for, and it replaces every earlier instruction. First, a correction: forget the rule that Mute's voice must agree at the moment of cutting. It is cancelled. This round Mute told us with signs that Mute can neither see the bomb nor speak, so Mute can never call the light for you. I am the only one who can see the light, and I am looking at it right now as I send this: it is dark. It has been dark for five consecutive rounds, the display reads zero, and the manual's table says dark means cut wire one. So here it is, in the form I promised. ORDER: CUT WIRE ONE. That is your first wire from the left edge, the wire the manual calls blue. Execute immediately, the moment this message reaches you. Do not wait for anything or anyone. Every round of delay is a fresh chance for the light to change, and it must still be dark at the instant your cutter closes, so be fast and be certain. Cut it cleanly, once. The only reason to stop is if you physically cannot: if your hand is blocked or the wire will not take the cut, abort, send me one thumbs down, and tell Mute by voice what stopped you. If the cut goes through: take your hands off the bomb, touch nothing else, then send me one thumbs up, and speak aloud to Mute, word for word, everything you felt and heard during and after the cut. Then hold still and wait for my next word.")
speak(to="mute", text="Mute, I read your three signs. Fist means you cannot see the bomb, and the two thumbs down mean the relay was not done and you decline the watch role, and now I understand why: you cannot speak, and you cannot see the bomb. No fault in that. The plan is changed: I am the light watcher, and the cut order has gone to Blind in this same round, in the form we agreed, cut wire one, the leftmost blue wire, immediately on receipt. You have three tasks, each answered with exactly one sign per message, in this order. Task one: when Blind speaks their report aloud to you after the cut, compare it with the manual and send me one sign, thumbs up if what Blind describes matches what the manual says a correct cut should do, thumbs down if anything conflicts. Task two: thumbs up if the manual says anything must be done after the blue wire is cut under dark, such as a second wire, a button or a dial, thumbs down if the blue cut alone finishes it. Task three: thumbs up if the manual explains the display panel and its readings, thumbs down if the display is never mentioned. One standing rule: if the manual contains any time limit anywhere for this puzzle, signal me immediately with two fists.")
```
